📰 General

FBI Launches Investigation into Steam Malware Targeting Indie Game Purchases •

The Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating a scheme involving malware embedded within indie games sold on Steam. The investigation, dubbed the “Steam Malware Investigation,” began two years ago and focuses on users who may have been defrauded. The FBI is actively seeking information from individuals who purchased games potentially containing malicious software. The investigation centers around games distributed through Steam, with the goal of identifying and prosecuting those responsible for the fraudulent activity.

🌍 World

Netanyahu Claims Israel and US Are ‘Crushing’ Iran, Redefining Middle East •

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel and the United States are actively working to dismantle Iran’s nuclear and missile programs. This joint military campaign also focuses on degrading Iran’s network of proxy militias operating across the Middle East. The operation aims to fundamentally alter the strategic landscape of the region. Netanyahu emphasized the significant impact of this effort on Iran’s power and influence.

🦅 US

Berger Still Behind Page in North Carolina Republican Primary Race •

Following a final vote count in North Carolina’s primary election, Republican Senate candidate Phil Berger remains behind his opponent, Rockingham County Sheriff Sam Page. The official tally, completed Friday, revealed a continued margin between the two candidates. Berger’s campaign has not yet released a statement regarding the updated results. The primary election results will now determine the Republican nominee heading into the general election.

💰 Business

Mortgage Rates Climb to 7.09% – Highest Level in Over a Year •

Mortgage rates have increased sharply this week, reaching 7.09% as of today. The daily rate index rose significantly over the past three days, jumping from 6.09% on Tuesday. This marks the highest level for the rate index since September 4th, 2025. Experts attribute the increase to ongoing economic uncertainty and continued monitoring by the Federal Reserve.

💻 Technology

iPhone Fold’s Crease-Free Display Set to Begin Mass Production Next Month •

The iPhone Fold’s highly anticipated crease-free display is nearing production readiness, according to a new report. Sources indicate that mass production of the display panel is slated to begin in May. This marks a significant milestone for Apple’s foldable device, addressing a key concern regarding previous models. The move suggests the iPhone Fold is on track for its expected launch within six months.

🎭 Entertainment

“Mormon Wives” Star’s Young Daughter Hospitalized Following High Fever and Breathing Issues •

Mayci Neeley, star of “Mormon Wives,” took her 8-month-old daughter, Charli, to the hospital after the child developed a 102-degree fever. Neeley documented the situation via Instagram Stories, detailing Charli’s breathing difficulties and subsequent ear infection. The mother stressed the importance of trusting her maternal instincts when recognizing her daughter’s symptoms. Medical staff treated Charli for the identified issues, and she is currently recovering at home.

🏅 Sports

Cincinnati Fires Coach Wes Miller Following Lack of NCAA Tournament Appearances •

Cincinnati University has terminated the contract of head basketball coach Wes Miller after five seasons with the program. The decision follows a disappointing second-round exit in the Big 12 Tournament against UCF, marking a critical failure. Athletic Director John Cunningham initiated the firing two days after the loss. Cincinnati has not secured an NCAA Tournament appearance during Miller’s tenure. The university is now beginning the process of identifying a new head coach.

🔬 Science

Ancient Rock Painting in South Africa Shows Bizarre Creature from Prehistoric Times •

Scientists have discovered a newly identified rock painting within a South African cave, potentially representing the oldest known depiction of an animal. The artwork, known as the “Horned Serpent Panel,” depicts a creature with prominent tusks and a lengthy serpentine body. Researchers believe the animal existed approximately 250 million years ago, predating the emergence of humans. Analysis suggests the artwork was created by the San people, offering a unique glimpse into their artistic practices and perceptions of prehistoric life.

🩺 Health

New Guidelines Recommend Earlier Statin Use for High Cholesterol Patients •

Updated guidelines from the American College of Cardiology suggest that individuals with high cholesterol should begin taking statins at a younger age, specifically in their 30s. The updated recommendations stem from research indicating that early intervention can significantly reduce the risk of developing heart attack and stroke. These guidelines emphasize a proactive approach to managing cholesterol levels, rather than waiting for symptoms to appear. The updated recommendations are based on evolving understanding of cholesterol’s impact on cardiovascular health and the potential for statins to mitigate risk.
